subject.title: [Bug/Docs]: local+hybrid memory_search quality can appear unstable due to extraPaths path drift + benchmark-file contamination

question: Should OpenClaw ship a narrow builtin-only memorySearch.excludePaths contract now, or wait for a shared cross-backend recall/index path-scope contract?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the durable API affects public config, indexed memory state, QMD parity, diagnostics, and documentation promises.

options.title: Ship builtin-only after repair
options.body: Fix the active PR's matcher issue, keep default behavior unchanged, document the QMD caveat, and track QMD/path-drift diagnostics separately.

options.title: Require shared path scopes
options.body: Hold the exclusion key until builtin indexing, QMD collections, watcher behavior, recall eligibility, and diagnostics share one include/exclude model.

options.title: Docs and diagnostics first
options.body: Defer public exclusion config and focus on path-drift, broad-extraPaths, and benchmark-contamination guidance plus stronger status warnings.

recommendation.title: Ship builtin-only after repair
recommendation.body: Fix the active PR's matcher issue, keep default behavior unchanged, document the QMD caveat, and track QMD/path-drift diagnostics separately.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across memory host internals and the published memory docs touched by this product/config decision.
